subject: POC kickoff — technical runway, capacity, and hands-on session
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — technical runway, capacity, and hands-on session

Thanks Kate — excited to get Orion Analytics up and running. High level proposal: schedule a 90-minute hands-on kickoff where we do a quick walkthrough, prompt review, routing decision (hosted vs dedicated), and a short load-test window to validate token budgeting and rate limits.

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue Apr 16, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Apr 17, 14:00–15:30
- Thu Apr 18, 09:00–10:30

Agenda (draft):
1) Intros and goals (10m)
2) Prompt & eval scope — examples you want to run (20m)
3) Routing and model variant discussion (hosted vs dedicated) (20m)
4) Load-test run (10–15m) + token budget check (15m)
5) Action items & next steps (10m)

Two operational questions for you before we lock a time:
- Will you want us to provision a short-term quota bump for the load test (yes/no)? If yes, approximate QPS you expect for the 15-min window.
- Any constraints on the test data (PII, internal-only)? If sensitive, we'll provision a private VPC trial.

I'll include Marissa (CS) and Ben (SE) — they'll own the hands-on flow and the load script. I attached a short runbook (POC-Runbook.pdf) and a token-budget template for your planning.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Quick answers to your ops questions:
- Yes to a quota bump for the load window. We expect a short spike of ~70 QPS for the 15-minute run (we'll stagger users).
- Data: some examples contain hashed PII; nothing that requires air-gapped handling but we'd prefer an isolated trial if it's not a big lift.

Can you confirm whether dedicated capacity will be necessary for that QPS, or if a hosted trial with a temporary higher tier suffices? Also looping in our procurement contact to confirm contract / trial terms.

Folks — adding the technical prep notes so you can review ahead of Wed. Key points:
- For a 70 QPS spike for 15 minutes with typical multi-turn prompts (avg 450 tokens/request) we estimate ~630k tokens across the window. Hosted with a temporary quota bump should be fine if we raise burst QPS and token cap; fallback plan is a minimal dedicated pool (1x A10 equivalent) during the spike.
- Rate limits: default hosted limits are 50 QPS per org; we can request a short increase to ~120 QPS during the test. If we hit rate limit errors, the runtime will retry with exponential backoff — but that impacts latency SLOs.
- Routing: we'll demo model variants that bias for deterministic output first (quantized mid-size model), then show a higher-capacity variant for throughput.

Attached: rate_limits_summary.txt with quick commands to monitor errors and the load script stub (links in drive).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
